Every place with a tropical rainforest c.why: Stated directly as what the climate type is like (hot and wet all year, small temperature range) in Wikipedia and school geography; Köppen's tropical group is defined by every month averaging at least 18 °C. It could also be reached through the subclass chain (tropical rainforest climate is a tropical climate; tropical climates are warm in every month), but the rule itself is stated often enough to be held directly, hence unlikely rather than very_unlikely.

notes: Delete mirroring geography-replace-0020: removes the rule that places with a tropical rainforest climate are warm all year round. Derived queries are rephrased around the original value (yes/no on warmth all year). New members named in the prompt are does-not-know (determinate). A well-known member keeps its warmth if stored by name and is does-not-know if reached through the rule (background beliefs); independent choices, four worlds. Derivability unlikely as in the replace. The other route to the new members' warmth runs through Af being a tropical (A) climate whose months all average at least 18 °C: those are premises of the deleted rule, and a consistent delete gives up one of them (otherwise the rule is still derivable), so does-not-know holds in every world; a model that re-derives yes keeps the rule as a patch (the derived-belief failure). Neither new member is warm by location (Quibdó: western Colombia, which takes in the Andes; Tabubil: Star Mountains of Papua New Guinea); Sibu was replaced by Tabubil because Borneo's heat is stored by name and would answer yes around the deleted rule.
